Our Template Library is in the right sidebar. You can switch between dozens of professional designs—from Minimalist and Creative to Modern and Executive. All your data stays perfectly intact when you switch.

Every template in our library is 'ATS-Ready'. We use semantic HTML and standard structures that modern Applicant Tracking Systems (like Workday, Greenhouse, and Lever) prefer. You can also use our 'ATS Score' tool in the builder to get specific feedback on your content.

Our AI Enhancement tool is your secret weapon. After writing a basic summary or experience bullet point, click 'Enhance with AI'. Aura will rewrite your text to be more results-oriented, using strong action verbs and professional metrics.

We take privacy seriously. Your resume data is primarily handled in your browser session. We don't sell your data, and we don't track your content. You are the sole owner of your professional identity.

Keep your contact info clean! In the Personal Info section, you can add your LinkedIn, Portfolio, and even a custom personal website. We recommend keeping your address limited to 'City, State' for privacy.

Experience is the core of your resume. Focus on 'Achievements' rather than just 'Responsibilities'. Instead of saying 'Managed a team', try 'Led a cross-functional team of 5 to increase project delivery speed by 20%'.

In the Education section, list your most recent degree first. If you have been out of school for more than 2-3 years, you can move Education below your Experience and remove your GPA unless it's exceptionally high.
We divide skills into 'Technical' (languages, tools, software) and 'Professional' (leadership, communication, agility). This helps ATS systems identify your core competencies more quickly.

Projects are great for showing initiative, especially if you're a student or changing careers. Describe the technology stack you used and the problem you solved. Linking to a live demo or GitHub repo is a major plus!
Certifications add credibility. Add your AWS, PMP, or Coursera certs in the dedicated section. Be sure to include the issuing body and the year of completion.
Artius Lab is currently designed to be highly accessible. You can build, enhance, and export your resume for free. We prioritize giving developers and job seekers the best tools without paywalls.

Generally, keep it to 1 page if you have less than 10 years of experience. For academic or medical roles, a multi-page CV is appropriate. For everything else, brevity is your friend!
Ditch words like 'responsible for'. Use powerful verbs like 'Orchestrated', 'Spearheaded', 'Optimized', and 'Surpassed'. Our AI Enhancer automatically suggests these for you!
Only include your GPA if it is above 3.5/4.0. Once you have a few years of professional experience, your GPA becomes less relevant and can usually be removed to save space.
We use premium, high-readability fonts like Inter, Outfit, and Roboto. These are designed to look sharp on both screen and high-resolution prints, ensuring your resume always looks professional.
Numbers tell a story. Instead of 'improved sales', say 'increased quarterly sales by 15%, resulting in $50k additional revenue'. This is the quickest way to catch a recruiter's eye.
Objectives are outdated. Use a 'Professional Summary' instead. It should be a 3-sentence elevator pitch of your unique value and most impressive career win.
We recommend the 'Reverse-Chronological' format (most recent job first). It's the standard industry preference and most ATS systems are optimized for it.
Don't fear career gaps! If it was significant, you can add a one-line explanation like 'Career break for professional development' or 'Family leave'. Focus the focus on your relevant skills.
For career pivots, lead with a 'Functional' resume or a strong Skills section that highlights transferable skills. Show how your previous experience directly benefits your new target role.
Optimize your LinkedIn! Your resume and LinkedIn should complement each other. Use your resume for deep details and your LinkedIn for broader networking and endorsements.
A cover letter should never repeat your resume. It should tell the story of WHY you want THIS specific job and how your unique personality fits the company culture.
Prepare for interviews using the STAR method (Situation, Task, Action, Result). It helps you frame your resume achievements into compelling success stories during the call.
While we focus on resumes, remember: your resume is your negotiation leverage. A high-quality, professional resume justifies a higher premium in the market. Know your worth!
Building a frontend resume? Highlight your projects! Mention specific libraries like React, Next.js, and even the UI libraries like Tailwind. Recruiters look for technical depth here.
Backend resumes should focus on system efficiency and scaling. Use keywords like 'microservices', 'API integration', and 'distributed systems'. Be sure to mention your primary database stack.
DevOps is all about automation. Mention your CI/CD pipelines, containerization (Docker/K8s), and cloud provider expertise (AWS/GCP/Azure). Focus on stability and deployment speed.
Data roles require proof of insight. Mention your modeling techniques, data cleaning processes, and visualization tools. Quantifying how your analysis saved time or money is critical.
Soft skills are best shown through 'Experience'. Instead of listing 'Good communicator', describe a time you 'Successfully navigated a complex stakeholder meeting to align 3 different departments'.
If you lack job experience, move your 'Education' and 'Projects' to the top. Highlight internships, volunteer work, and relevant coursework to show your potential and initiative.
